stem: A 7-year-old is found to have a low white cell count on a routine blood test; before deciding that the result is abnormal, which principle should be applied first?

options.text: Interpret the white cell count against the child's age
Assume any low white cell count reflects leukaemia
Focus only on whether the platelet count is normal
Ignore the result if the child appears well
Use the adult reference range because it is more standardised

explanation: Interpret the white cell count against the child's age. White cell count varies with age, so paediatric results should be compared with age-appropriate reference ranges before deciding that the result is truly abnormal.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: WBC Disorders

optionExplanations.A: Correct because white cell count varies with age and should be interpreted using age-appropriate reference ranges.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a low white cell count does not automatically mean leukaemia; age and the overall clinical context must be considered.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because platelet count may be useful for broader interpretation, but it does not replace age-based assessment of the white cell count.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a reassuring appearance does not make an abnormal laboratory result irrelevant.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because adult reference ranges are not appropriate for children, whose white cell counts vary with age.
